quest.title: A Path Through the Storm
quest.description: You share your feelings with Paimon before embarking on the next phase of your journey.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x700, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Take in the view outside of Liyue Harbor to collect your thoughts

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Are you okay? Paimon never imagined your {F#brother}{M#sister} would have sided with the Abyss...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, keep your chin up, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon believes in both of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And when the going gets tough, the tough get going! Right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{F#He}{M#She} said we needed to "reach the end of our journey..." Paimon bets {F#he}{M#she} still has lots more to tell us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And we won't find out what this "journey" is or where it will end unless we keep going!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, don't mention it, partner! Travel buddies are supposed to look out for one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although... where should we go next? If we want to continue with the journey... hmm...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I still need to find that god...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh! You mean, the god that took your {F#brother}{M#sister} away in the first place...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You're right. After all, everything that followed... all this confusion... it all started with her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon bets she's the key to understanding this whole mystery.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we've ruled out two gods so far — the Anemo and Geo Archons. So, next...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon doesn't think we can simply walk into Inazuma. Zhongli said it was a closed nation. We'll have to find some other way in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we ask someone from Inazuma how to gain entrance?

choices.text: Let me try and think of someone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon's thought of someone already — Atsuko, in Liyue Harbor! She's from Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see what she has to say!

choices.text: I'm sure there is someone we've met...
I need to teach her a lesson she won't forget.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon supports that idea! Just the thought of it is so satisfying!

choices.text: I'm glad to have you as a guide, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee, then Paimon will be sure to keep up the good work!

choices.text: There must be more to this than meets the eye.

talks.objective: Ask Atsuko about how to travel to Inazuma

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Hello... Oh! I—I mean, good fortune... right? *sigh* I'm still learning to talk like a local, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We wanted to ask... how do we get into Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Ohh, so that's why you're here... Well, there is a way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! We came to the right person!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But the chance of success is... incredibly small.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Incredibly small? Then how did you get out of Inazuma in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It was in leaving Inazuma that I found out just how dangerous this method truly was...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: All I had to rely on was a little wooden raft that I'd put together myself. There was a storm raging ahead of me, and my pursuers were close on my tail.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: After I'd escaped their clutches, I floated on the open ocean for... I don't know how many days. My rations and fresh water supply soon ran out, and I remember getting to the point where I was sure I'd reached the end. Then, I blacked out.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But, to my surprise, my journey didn't end there... or to put it another way, a new beginning found me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did someone from Liyue save you?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That's right! I escaped by the skin of my teeth. The fact that I'm even alive to tell the tale must be a sign that the gods were watching over me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a horrible journey! And you set off knowing how dangerous it was? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Well... because everything is just too restrictive over there. The atmosphere is so stifling... The Kanjou Commission subjects everyone leaving or entering the nation to a protracted approval process, and... I felt like I didn't belong there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kanjou Commission? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Along with the other two commissions, they oversee everything in Inazuma. We usually collectively refer to them as the Tri-Commission — I suppose they're equivalent to the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: One of the obligations of the Kanjou Commission is to conduct rigorous identity checks on all individuals leaving or entering Inazuma. All non-nationals are processed centrally on Ritou upon arrival...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, the Tenryou Commission is responsible for implementing the recently promulgated Vision Hunt Decree. They act like the executive arm of the Raiden Shogun's rule, loyal yet unfeeling.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It doesn't feel good to speak ill of my home like this... but after spending so long under that oppressive atmosphere, I began to lose all hope for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: What I mean to say is... unless you have an extremely compelling reason to go to Inazuma, you should abandon your plans of trying to get there.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: *sigh* You should know that the sea around Inazuma is engulfed in a perpetual tempest of wind and rain. Supposing you survived that, you would still need to get past the samurai guards that enforce the Sakoku Decree — the closed nation policy of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: And even if you did manage to find a way, you'd still have to produce the necessary documentation at the Ritou center for processing outlanders. Otherwise, you'd be kicked out immediately...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like they really don't want anyone setting foot in Inazuma, huh...

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: They only set that up as a port to guarantee a supply of goods and information to the island. Most outlanders would be unable to acquire the documentation needed.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: But if you really are set on going, there is one thing you could try...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... The raft idea sounds a little on the dangerous side... plus Paimon would definitely get seasick.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: That's not what I meant. You could ask someone from The Crux Fleet if they have some way of getting you to Inazuma, they're well-known in Liyue.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Voyaging far and wide has made them a well-traveled group with a wide range of experiences. They may just know how to break through the storm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... it's an armed fleet, right? Why would they agree to a request like this?

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: That part is up to you! If you're able to persuade their captain, Beidou, then the hardest part will be out of the way.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: The Alcor is the flagship of The Crux Fleet. I heard that it's currently anchored by Guyun Stone Forest on a supply run. This might be your best chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then there's no time to lose! Let's go find Captain Beidou!

choices.text: It seems like our only option.
But there's a place for outlanders to go, right?
There are answers to questions I must know there.

talks.objective: Go to The Alcor and meet with Beidou

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #Hmm? Who've we got here... Wait, I know you. You're that traveler, {NICKNAME}, aren't you? The one who fought against the Fatui and Osial, right?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Haha, Ningguang told me about you. "A traveler of great insight and remarkable skill has saved Liyue," she said.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: She's a hard one to please... so praise from her is high praise indeed. I remember thinking at the time that it'd be good to meet you in person.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Judging by the clothes on your back and this floating thing, I guess that time has come.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! The name's not "floating thing," it's PAIMON!
Paimon... hmm... What a fascinating being. You two give off not only the essence of wind and earth, but also of... yes... the stars...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? The fragrance of what now? That's the weirdest compliment Paimon's ever heard...
Pay it no heed... I mean only to say I am certain... that it is by fate, not chance alone, that we should meet... and that gives our encounter meaning.

choices.text: Is this guy a bard, by any chance?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: You're not far off, but they go by a different name in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Uh, I prefer... other means of entertainment.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: This young man is Kaedehara Kazuha, a temporary addition to my crew for reasons I won't bore you with. Occasionally, he opens his mouth and flowers come out instead of words.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: With this fine ship and the soft sea breeze... would it not be romantically irresponsible of me not to acknowledge it with a line or two of poetry?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Haha, can't argue with that... Okay then, once The Clash is underway, I'll give you a chance to perform.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Only if the mood takes me, of course. Poetry for poetry's sake tends to lack meaning.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Hey, you don't wanna pass this opportunity up too easily, especially seeing as our great hero here might be in attendance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, what's The Clash? Also, just to clarify, by "great hero"... do you mean...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Huh? I thought you might be here to sign up... You're telling me you've never even heard of it?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: The Crux Clash is a martial arts tournament that I hold. There'll be a whole bunch of folks taking part to showcase their talents.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: There are two important rules. One — competitors must be renowned fighters. We want those with real martial arts ability, not just people taking part for the fun of it.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: So, you've got nothing to worry about there. I don't think there's anyone out there who hasn't heard of you.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Two — you can't take part if you've got a Vision. Otherwise, things get a little... one-sided.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't have a Vision, but—

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Haha, you must be feeling confident, but you might wanna watch out — there are a few crouching tigers and hidden dragons lurking around in Liyue.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: And with Liyue's savior taking part in the tournament... now that's gonna turn a few heads. I think we can expect a healthy turnout this time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... we didn't come here to take part in a martial arts tournament.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Well, before you dismiss the idea completely, you might be interested to hear that the prize this time 'round is particularly sought after...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Get this — it's a Masterless Vision!

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Supplied by myself, as a matter of fact. If the tournament champion can reawaken that Vision... it belongs to them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is there really such thing as a masterless Vision!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why doesn't it have a master?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: When a Vision bearer dies, the light in their Vision will fade away. But the shell that housed that light remains.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: As for whether this shell has any practical application, well, this remains to be seen. But my intuition tells me that while it remains in the world, it may just be possible for someone else to inherit it.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Yep, and the way I see it, a Vision is a badge of recognition from the gods — so if anyone's able to rekindle it, it's got to be an individual of exceptional strength and talent.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Organizing The Clash is my way of uncovering hidden talents... and hopefully, this time, of getting a Vision to glow again.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: So, if you don't have a Vision, this is the perfect opportunity to get your hands on one of your very own.

choices.text: To be honest, I'm not interested.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we're interested in getting to Inazuma, not fighting in some tournament!

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Inazuma? You... want to go there?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Well, why didn't you say so! Inazuma? No sweat.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: In that case, if you win the tournament, I'll give you a choice: Masterless Vision, or a ticket to Inazuma aboard The Alcor. Up to you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That was easy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You just want {F#her}{M#him} to take part in your tournament!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Hahaha, what's wrong with that? The more talent we have, the better the tournament will be. I couldn't let a competitor like you fall through the net.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What're we gonna do, {NICKNAME}? *sigh* Looks like we pretty much have to do this tournament if we want to get to Inazuma, huh?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Great, then, let's get you signed up! Head to the tournament arena in Guyun Stone Forest. Kazuha and I will be over soon.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: It seems like it will only be a matter of time before the answer is revealed...

choices.text: A Vision is of no use to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, are you here to compete in The Crux Clash?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: You bet I am, have you put your names down yet?

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Well, I'd have a look at the entrance criteria if I were you. They don't allow just anyone to take part.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: The Clash is a comprehensive test of fighting ability. Anyone who turns up for show over skill is gonna get their butt handed to them.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Tsk, nobody wants to see that, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we heard a rule about that. So Paimon's wondering... are you a renowned fighter?

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Hahaha, me? Only a former runner-up in the Chihu Rock Freestyle Combat Summit! Oh yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... Also, that doesn't sound like the most official tournament out there...

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: What!? You... Nonsense! Have you been living under a rock? It's been going on for years! There were plenty of competitors when I took part!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Not to mention, I've helped the Millelith catch Treasure Hoarders before! There were two of them trying to escape — I soon sorted them out.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: They tried to sneak past me under the cover of darkness... Ha! They didn't know what hit 'em.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I planted a left hook on the skinnier one's face and sent him flying. Then, the big guy pulled out a knife!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I stood my ground, of course. A roundhouse kick sent the blade hurtling into a beam above us.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Hahaha, I told you! Unarmed, outnumbered two to one, but I still got the upper hand!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I'm not saying I came out completely unscathed of course, but the fact remains that I did manage to subdue the both of them... AND hand them over to the Millelith. I received quite the commendation! Oh yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... But for us, even four or five Treasure Hoarders at a time is all in a day's work...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for letting us know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm... Alright, we're gonna keep looking around.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I'll see you in the arena. Tsk, but I don't plan on losing to a pair of children any time soon!

choices.text: We just wanted to take a look around first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, are you here for The Crux Clash too?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: That's right. Nothing beats real-life combat for honing your skills. That's what our master taught us.

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: But this tournament is more than just a chance to put training into practice — it's also a chance for us to obtain the Masterless Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Exactly! With a Vision, we'd quickly become our master's top students.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This master of yours must be pretty incredible, huh... Are they someone famous?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: Famous? He's the founder of the Lingshan Clan, and his skills are unparalleled! Liang and I are both proud disciples of his.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: You probably wouldn't have heard of it, it was founded quite recently. The clan is nowhere near as famous as the master himself, anyway.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: He's got to be a grandmaster or something. He's created many different styles of kung fu, and countless other clans have borrowed extensively from him.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: To the Lingshan Clan, he teaches a special technique known as "force dispersal."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Force dispersal"?

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It's a type of breathing exercise where you can train yourself to harness the energy around you and neutralize attacks without moving an inch.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: For example, our master can use it to alter the path of an attacking fist, or change the direction of an incoming stone, all without breaking a sweat!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: One time, he sent a challenger flying into the air without lifting a finger!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that really possible?

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It sure is! But it's extremely difficult to cultivate this ability. We've been training for ages, and we're still getting to grips with the very basics. There's no way we could use it proficiently yet.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: *sigh* We're clearly not that naturally gifted, or we would have at least gotten the gist by now... If we don't start making progress soon, we'll probably run out of money to pay the tuition fees and still have nothing to show for all our training...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a tuition fee!?

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Of course! This is a grandmaster we're talking about here. He doesn't have time to waste. If you want face-to-face training, you've gotta show you're sincere about it.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: *sigh* But here we are, having trained under him directly all this time without even a hint of improvement. Master is getting increasingly impatient with us.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Recently, though, we heard that a Vision bearer joined the Guhua Clan and made pretty much instant progress in their training.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: So, if we can get our hands on a Vision, too, maybe we can finally make our master proud!

choices.text: A Vision won't make you better at martial arts.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Well, we have to try something new, otherwise, we're stuck in the same situation.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Exactly, it can't hurt to try. And if it turns out it does work, the Lingshan Clan will go down in history!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Folks will come from far and wide. Heck, we could even become the dominant martial arts clan in all of Liyue!

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: See you in the arena!

choices.text: There may be other reasons why you can't seem to master this technique...

dialogues.speaker: Jinyou
dialogues.text: Hey, youngster. Are you here for The Crux Clash too?

dialogues.speaker: Jinyou
dialogues.text: If so... seems I've found myself another new adversary.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're also here for the tournament?

dialogues.speaker: Jinyou
dialogues.text: You better believe it. I wouldn't be here if I didn't think I could walk away as a champion.

dialogues.speaker: Jinyou
dialogues.text: For me, obtaining a Vision is the final and most important piece in the puzzle that is my life.

choices.text: Do you want to become an adventurer?

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: No, no, no — it's not about what I want to do. This is about who I want to be. I am looking to become a perfect person.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: I know how that sounds, but let me explain. I've lived a successful life so far, without any setbacks.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: I've passed every exam I've ever taken, enjoyed numerous successful business ventures, and seem to get on with just about everyone socially...

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: In most people's eyes, I am already the very embodiment of the perfect person, though of course, I'd never let the praise get to my head. I know I haven't reached perfection yet... because there's one thing I'm still missing...

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: ...A Vision.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have so much self-confidence...

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: That's not important... I have a contact in The Crux Fleet who was happy to vouch for me. So, they very kindly made special arrangements on my behalf.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: I've also brought along a bit of an entourage, for moral support. It's such a blessing, really, to have so many good friends in my neighborhood.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: Of course, I also put in a few good days' practice, concentrating mostly on rare and esoteric styles of kung fu. As a high-achiever by nature, I'm confident I've done enough to guarantee my victory in this tournament.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: Hah, you don't mince your words, do you... The arena will be the judge.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: Now then, if you don't mind, I need to finish my pre-competition routine. It's not too long now before you'll get to see me in action.

response.speaker: Jinyou
response.text: Haha, I seem to have gained another fan. Don't let my aura overwhelm you, though. You'll need your wits about you today.

choices.text: Do you want to become a hero?

talks.objective: Talk to Zhuhan, who is in charge of registration for The Crux Clash

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Qingce Village Armwrestling Champion, huh... *sigh* Alright, you're signed up...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Next please... what's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Wait! A—Aren't you...!?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #Did I hear that right? {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: Is it really them?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Aren't they a Vision bearer, though? Why are they trying to enter The Clash?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Uh... I—I have to ask... aren't you the traveler that helped Liyue fight off that ancient god...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #It's really {F#her}{M#him}!

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: The one that spoke with Lady Keqing at the Rite of Parting!

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #Oh! Oh! I wonder if I can get {F#her}{M#his} autograph later?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: I—I trust you are aware that... only those without Visions can enter the tournament?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't have a Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Really? B—But from what I've heard, the things you're capable of in combat are... nothing short of extraordinary... You walk into the most dangerous situations imaginable, face off against all sorts of monsters — even the Fatui — and always come out on top!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yup! {F#She}{M#He} still doesn't have a Vision though. See for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: My apologies, I didn't mean to be rude. I'm sure a great hero like yourself would have no reason to lie. Now, could I ask you to provide a few claims to fame?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: It's just a formality for you, of course, but I have to make a record of competitors' achievements as part of the sign-up process...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: So far I've got "Defeated the ancient god, Osial," so that's one. Do you... have any others?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and also a dragon, too! Put down "Battle with Stormterror"!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: #Might as well declare {F#her}{M#him} the champion already.

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: I wonder if it's too late to withdraw?

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Okay, um... that's plenty... Actually, this is the most dazzling track record I've ever seen, by a long shot...

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Right, your registration is complete. Now, a brief word about the prize.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: A great hero such as yourself can surely only be here for one thing — to win the tournament and claim the grand prize, namely, a Vision.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we're not here for that. We're here because Captain Beidou promised to take us to Inazuma if we win the tournament.

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: There's another prize too? First I've heard of it!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: Beidou must have upped the stakes this time to attract top talent!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: But why would anyone want to go somewhere as dangerous as Inazuma?

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: ...I see, so... I take it you discussed your terms with Beidou in advance, then.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Well, nobody expected you to sign up to a tournament like this... I can hardly believe it myself, to be honest...

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Anyway, the qualifying rounds are about to begin. I'll leave you to your preparation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, so, Paimon's thinking about that whole "no Vision bearers" rule in this tournament.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though you don't have a Vision, most people in Teyvat think that you can't manipulate the elements without one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Paimon thinks you probably shouldn't use your elemental abilities during the tournament. Y'know, just to avoid any misunderstandings.

choices.text: I'm just not that interested in Visions, that's all.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Well, I'm sure a great hero has an important reason for being here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, put that down! And also, "Defeated the Fatui Harbinger, Childe."

choices.text: I'm the Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Also, don't forget to mention that previous battles include, but are not limited to "Stormterror" Dvalin and Fatui Harbinger, Childe.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Best of luck to you in your journey to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Oh, and if you do actually make it to Inazuma, please be sure not to mention my name to anyone there.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Go on, get yourself to Guyun and sign up already.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I've already fixed up the arena. You can't miss it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Martial arts tournaments always remind me of the duels they have back in Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But when the combatants are obliged to exercise restraint, it is unlikely they will ever display their true potential.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Hello... Oh! I—I mean, good fortune... right? *sigh* I'm still learning to talk like a local, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We wanted to ask... how do we get into Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Ohh, so that's why you're here... Well, there is a way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! We came to the right person!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But the chance of success is... incredibly small.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Incredibly small? Then how did you get out of Inazuma in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It was in leaving Inazuma that I found out just how dangerous this method truly was...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: All I had to rely on was a little wooden raft that I'd put together myself. There was a storm raging ahead of me, and my pursuers were close on my tail.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: After I'd escaped their clutches, I floated on the open ocean for... I don't know how many days. My rations and fresh water supply soon ran out, and I remember getting to the point where I was sure I'd reached the end. Then, I blacked out.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But, to my surprise, my journey didn't end there... or to put it another way, a new beginning found me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did someone from Liyue save you?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That's right! I escaped by the skin of my teeth. The fact that I'm even alive to tell the tale must be a sign that the gods were watching over me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a horrible journey! And you set off knowing how dangerous it was? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Well... because everything is just too restrictive over there. The atmosphere is so stifling... The Kanjou Commission subjects everyone leaving or entering the nation to a protracted approval process, and... I felt like I didn't belong there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kanjou Commission? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Along with the other two commissions, they oversee everything in Inazuma. We usually collectively refer to them as the Tri-Commission — I suppose they're equivalent to the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: One of the obligations of the Kanjou Commission is to conduct rigorous identity checks on all individuals leaving or entering Inazuma. All non-nationals are processed centrally on Ritou upon arrival...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, the Tenryou Commission is responsible for implementing the recently promulgated Vision Hunt Decree. They act like the executive arm of the Raiden Shogun's rule, loyal yet unfeeling.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It doesn't feel good to speak ill of my home like this... but after spending so long under that oppressive atmosphere, I began to lose all hope for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: What I mean to say is... unless you have an extremely compelling reason to go to Inazuma, you should abandon your plans of trying to get there.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: *sigh* You should know that the sea around Inazuma is engulfed in a perpetual tempest of wind and rain. Supposing you survived that, you would still need to get past the samurai guards that enforce the Sakoku Decree — the closed nation policy of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: And even if you did manage to find a way, you'd still have to produce the necessary documentation at the Ritou center for processing outlanders. Otherwise, you'd be kicked out immediately...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like they really don't want anyone setting foot in Inazuma, huh...

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: They only set that up as a port to guarantee a supply of goods and information to the island. Most outlanders would be unable to acquire the documentation needed.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: But if you really are set on going, there is one thing you could try...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... The raft idea sounds a little on the dangerous side... plus Paimon would definitely get seasick.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: That's not what I meant. You could ask someone from The Crux Fleet if they have some way of getting you to Inazuma, they're well-known in Liyue.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Voyaging far and wide has made them a well-traveled group with a wide range of experiences. They may just know how to break through the storm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right! I'm sure if we can get Beidou's help, she'll certainly find a way out of this mess. Her crew is super strong!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wonders if she'll be willing to take this risk...

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: The Alcor is the flagship of The Crux Fleet. I heard that it's currently anchored by Guyun Stone Forest on a supply run. This might be your best chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are we waiting for? Let's go find Beidou right away!

choices.text: It seems like our only option.
But there's a place for outlanders to go, right?
There are answers to questions I must know there.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #Oh? If it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I knew you guys would come, hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So to recap... we're up against an inflated ego, some gullible guys paying way too much for their kung fu classes, and another guy who's just... really average.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Seems like you've got a pretty good chance of winning this thing, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go sign up!
